── bwrap ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INCOMPLETE ON ITS OWN — the network namespace is NOT in this argv.
  The stage created it, pinned it, and a setns shim put bwrap inside it before
  bwrap ran, so no --unshare-net appears below. Nothing could appear in its
  place: bwrap takes --userns FD and --pidns FD, and has no --netns FD.
  RUN AS PRINTED, this command lands in YOUR network namespace and starts no
  pasta helper — host loopback and the host's abstract sockets (X11, D-Bus)
  are both reachable, every line of the NETWORK block above is false of what
  you ran, and what you measured is your own host network.
bwrap
  --ro-bind /usr /usr
  -- /bin/sh
(argv[0] is the bare name "bwrap" and snug does not exec that name: it calls
 exec.LookPath("bwrap") against the HOST user's own $PATH at the moment the
 run starts, and execs the absolute path that search returns. WHICH bwrap runs
 is therefore a fact about that $PATH then — a directory earlier on it than
 /usr/bin chooses the binary, after this artifact has said everything it has
 to say. Settle it by hand with: command -v bwrap)
(the argv ends here and the network namespace was never in it — see the note
 above it. To check the netns by hand, compare inside against outside:
     readlink /proc/self/ns/net                        # on the host
     snug -p @net <dir> -- readlink /proc/self/ns/net  # inside
 The two must DIFFER, and an empty answer from either side is a failed check
 rather than a pass: an empty string is != any real namespace id.)
